openai-curated.notes: Use inside Codex when the plugin/app is available and task scope is explicit.

openai-primary-runtime.notes: Use for local document, spreadsheet, and presentation artifacts.

openai-bundled.notes: Use for browser, chrome, and local bundled tools.

openai-codex.notes: Use for local coding workflow and Codex runtime patterns.

claude-plugins-official.notes: Use as Claude Code planning and skill routing metadata unless explicitly installed and scoped.

google-official-mcp.notes: Use for official Google docs or Google service planning after task scope is explicit; account-scoped actions require approval and stay under Google Open Source Copilot.

google-open-source.notes: Use Google-origin open-source projects as Google Open Source Copilot candidates until a concrete implementation need exists.

microsoft-official.notes: Use Microsoft official docs and verified open-source projects after task scope is explicit.

meta-official.notes: Use Meta open-source projects as candidates; prefer current repo architecture before adopting new runtime surfaces.

aws-official.notes: Use AWS official docs for planning; provisioning, deploys, and account reads require approval.

apple-official.notes: Use Apple open-source projects only for Apple-platform, Swift, WebKit, or compatibility work.

cloudflare-official.notes: Use Cloudflare docs and OSS for edge planning; deploys remain approval-gated.

vercel-official.notes: Use Vercel OSS and docs for Next.js/Turborepo alignment; production deploys remain approval-gated.

openai-official.notes: Use official OpenAI docs and SDKs for explicit AI feature scopes; model calls and secrets require approval.

big-tech-open-source.notes: Use major-firm open-source projects as a curated candidate matrix, not as default dependencies.

market-share-intelligence.notes: Use market-share and competitor-intelligence connectors as scoped analysis signals; paid data and account reads require approval.

local-mcp.notes: Use local read-only tools for validation and documentation lookup when they reduce implementation risk.

public-docs.notes: Use public official docs as fallback when an official MCP is unavailable or auth-blocked.

skills.notes: Language or SDK-specific skill cards stay registry-only until a concrete implementation task appears.
